title: Com'era?
summary: How things used to be: childhood habits, what was going on when something happened, and a city then and now. The imperfetto, and how it shares the past with the passato prossimo.
canDo: I can describe what I used to do and what things were like.
I can set the scene of a story and say what happened in it.
I can compare a place in the past with how it is now.

items.back: The imperfetto: habits, descriptions and ongoing situations in the past.
items.note: essere: ero, eri, era, eravamo, eravate, erano.
items.pt: Same job as the PT pretérito imperfeito: morava, era, fazia.
PT morar. "Vivere" also works; "abitare" is about your address.
PT frequentemente, muitas vezes. Not "espesso", which is "denso".

items.note: "Ogni" never changes: ogni giorno, ogni mattina.

items.back: to go for a swim; to have a bath
items.pt: PT tomar banho (de mar). Italian uses "fare".

items.note: Weather uses fare: fa freddo, fa caldo.
Pioveva = it was raining. Ha piovuto = it rained.

items.pt: PT parar de. "Parare" in Italian is what a goalkeeper does.
Close to PT "então". "Allora?" on its own is like "E aí?".
PT havia / tinha. Italian must agree with what follows.
PT ainda não: the order is reversed.

items.note: Singular: la gente prendeva il tram.
items.pt: False friend: PT "a gente" often means "nós". Italian "la gente" is always "as pessoas".

lessons.title: Da bambino…
lessons.canDo: I can say what I used to do and describe how things were.

intro.scene: At the bar, Giulia is showing Leo old photos on her phone.

lines.text: Guarda questa foto! Da bambina abitavo a Napoli.
lines.meaning: Look at this photo! As a child I lived in Naples.

lines.text: Davvero? E com'era la tua casa?
lines.meaning: Really? And what was your house like?

lines.text: Era piccola, ma aveva un balcone sul mare.
lines.meaning: It was small, but it had a balcony over the sea.

lines.text: Che bello! Andavi spesso in spiaggia?
lines.meaning: How lovely! Did you often go to the beach?

lines.text: Ogni giorno! D'estate facevamo il bagno fino a sera.
lines.meaning: Every day! In summer we swam until the evening.

lines.text: Io invece giocavo a calcio per strada tutti i giorni.
lines.meaning: I, on the other hand, played football in the street every day.

notes.title: The imperfetto
notes.body: Take off -re and add -vo, -vi, -va, -vamo, -vate, -vano: abitare → abitavo, avere → avevo, dormire → dormivo. It is the most regular tense in Italian. The main exceptions: essere (ero, eri, era, eravamo, eravate, erano), fare → facevo, dire → dicevo, bere → bevevo.

notes.title: When to use it
notes.body: For habits (andavo in spiaggia ogni giorno), descriptions (la casa era piccola) and anything that was ongoing, with no clear beginning or end.

notes.title: 🇧🇷 PT tip: same idea, different stress
notes.body: It lines up with the PT imperfeito: morava = abitavo, era = era, fazia = facevo. The trap is the sound. Italian stresses noi and voi on the "a": abitavAmo, abitavAte. And loro keeps the stress early: abitAvano, not *abitavAno.

exercises.text: Da bambino ___ a calcio tutti i giorni.
exercises.meaning: As a child I played football every day.
exercises.explain: A repeated habit in the past: imperfetto.

exercises.prompt: What is the imperfetto of "fare" for io?
exercises.explain: Fare keeps its old stem: facevo, facevi, faceva.

exercises.prompt: Build: "We went to the beach every day."
exercises.meaning: We went to the beach every day.

exercises.explain: Loro keeps the stress of the io form: abiTAvo, abiTAvano.

lessons.title: Mentre guardavo il telefono…
lessons.canDo: I can set the scene with the imperfetto and say what happened with the passato prossimo.

intro.scene: Marco was at the stadium last night. Leo wants every detail.

lines.text: Ieri sera ero allo stadio. Pioveva e faceva freddo.
lines.meaning: Last night I was at the stadium. It was raining and it was cold.
And the match? How did it go?

lines.text: Mentre guardavo il telefono, la Roma ha segnato!
lines.meaning: While I was looking at my phone, Roma scored!

lines.text: No! Non hai visto il gol?
lines.meaning: No! You didn't see the goal?

lines.text: No. Ma poi ha smesso di piovere e abbiamo vinto.
lines.meaning: No. But then it stopped raining and we won.

notes.title: Background and event
notes.body: The imperfetto paints the background: pioveva, faceva freddo, ero allo stadio. The passato prossimo says what happened, once and completely: la Roma ha segnato, abbiamo vinto.

notes.title: Mentre
notes.body: "Mentre" + imperfetto is the action in progress; the event that interrupts it is in the passato prossimo: mentre guardavo il telefono, la Roma ha segnato.

notes.title: 🇧🇷 PT tip: the split is the same
notes.body: Portuguese makes the same choice: "enquanto eu olhava o celular, a Roma marcou". So trust your instinct for which tense. Only the form is different: PT "marcou" is one word, Italian "ha segnato" is two. In conversation, never the one-word "segnò".

exercises.text: Mentre ___ la partita, è arrivato Marco.
exercises.meaning: While I was watching the match, Marco arrived.

exercises.text: Ieri la Roma ___ due a zero.

exercises.prompt: You are starting a story. Which sentence sets the scene?
exercises.explain: Weather and atmosphere are background: imperfetto.

exercises.prompt: Build: "While I was sleeping, Giulia called."
exercises.meaning: While I was sleeping, Giulia called.

exercises.explain: Smettere di + infinitive. "Parare" is to save a shot, not to stop.

exercises.prompt: Translate from Portuguese: "Fazia frio, mas nós ganhamos."
alt: Faceva freddo, ma noi abbiamo vinto.

lessons.title: Qui una volta c'era…
lessons.canDo: I can say what a place used to have and how it has changed.

intro.scene: Sara is walking Leo through the neighbourhood where her grandmother grew up.

lines.text: Vedi questa piazza? Una volta qui c'era un mercato.
lines.meaning: See this square? There used to be a market here.

lines.text: E adesso c'è solo un parcheggio. Che peccato!
lines.meaning: And now there's only a car park. What a pity!

lines.text: Mia nonna veniva qui ogni mattina. C'erano tanti banchi di frutta.
lines.meaning: My grandmother came here every morning. There were lots of fruit stalls.
And the metro? Was it already there?

lines.text: No, non c'era ancora. La gente prendeva il tram.
lines.meaning: No, it wasn't there yet. People took the tram.

notes.title: C'era, c'erano
notes.body: The imperfetto of c'è and ci sono: c'era un mercato (one thing), c'erano tanti banchi (several). Perfect for describing how a place used to be.

notes.title: Then and now
notes.body: "Una volta" and "allora" point to the past; "adesso" and "ora" to the present. "Già" is already, and "non… ancora" is not yet: non c'era ancora.

notes.title: 🇧🇷 PT tip: it has to agree
notes.body: Brazilian Portuguese says "tinha um mercado" and "tinha muitas bancas" with the same verb. Italian cannot: c'era for one, c'erano for many, and never "aveva". Also, "la gente" is singular and means "as pessoas", not "nós": la gente prendeva il tram.

exercises.meaning: There used to be a market here.

exercises.text: In piazza ___ tanti banchi di frutta.
exercises.meaning: In the square there were lots of fruit stalls.
exercises.explain: Several things: c'erano. "Aveva" would need an owner.

lessons.title: Lettura: Il quartiere di mia nonna
lessons.canDo: I can read a short text about the past and answer questions about it in Italian.

intro.scene: Un testo breve. Leggi, ascolta e poi rispondi alle domande.

sentences.text: Mia nonna Rosa è nata a Roma, nel quartiere di Testaccio.
sentences.meaning: My grandmother Rosa was born in Rome, in the Testaccio neighbourhood.

sentences.text: Da bambina abitava in una casa piccola, vicino al mercato.
sentences.meaning: As a child she lived in a small house near the market.

sentences.text: Ogni mattina andava a scuola a piedi con suo fratello.
sentences.meaning: Every morning she walked to school with her brother.

sentences.text: Nel quartiere non c'erano molte macchine e i bambini giocavano per strada.
sentences.meaning: There weren't many cars in the neighbourhood and the children played in the street.

sentences.text: La domenica tutta la famiglia mangiava insieme e poi ascoltava la partita alla radio.
sentences.meaning: On Sundays the whole family ate together and then listened to the match on the radio.

sentences.text: Un giorno, mentre tornava da scuola, Rosa ha trovato un cane.
sentences.meaning: One day, while she was coming home from school, Rosa found a dog.

sentences.text: Ha portato il cane a casa. Si chiamava Pippo.
sentences.meaning: She took the dog home. His name was Pippo.

sentences.text: Pippo è rimasto con la famiglia per quindici anni.
sentences.meaning: Pippo stayed with the family for fifteen years.

sentences.text: Oggi il mercato c'è ancora, ma mia nonna dice che allora il quartiere era più tranquillo.
sentences.meaning: Today the market is still there, but my grandmother says the neighbourhood was quieter back then.

options: A Roma, nel quartiere di Testaccio.

exercises.prompt: Perché i bambini giocavano per strada?
options: Perché le case erano troppo piccole.

exercises.prompt: Che cosa faceva la famiglia la domenica?
options: Mangiava insieme e ascoltava la partita alla radio.

exercises.prompt: Che cosa è successo un giorno, mentre Rosa tornava da scuola?
exercises.explain: The background is in the imperfetto (tornava); the event is in the passato prossimo (ha trovato).

exercises.prompt: Vero o falso? Oggi il mercato non c'è più.

meme.bottom: starts with "mia nonna" and ends with food or a dog

lessons.title: Racconto: La partita che non ho visto
lessons.canDo: I can follow a short spoken story in the past and answer questions about it in Italian.

intro.scene: Marco racconta la sua domenica. Ascolta bene: che cosa è successo, e in che ordine?

sentences.text: Domenica scorsa volevo guardare la partita a casa di Leo.
sentences.meaning: Last Sunday I wanted to watch the match at Leo's place.

sentences.text: Pioveva forte e l'autobus non arrivava.
sentences.meaning: It was raining hard and the bus wasn't coming.

sentences.text: Ho aspettato venti minuti, poi ho deciso di andare a piedi.
sentences.meaning: I waited twenty minutes, then I decided to walk.

sentences.text: Mentre camminavo, ho sentito un urlo dalle finestre: gol della Roma!
sentences.meaning: While I was walking, I heard a shout from the windows: a goal for Roma!

sentences.text: Quando sono arrivato, ero tutto bagnato e la partita era quasi finita.
sentences.meaning: When I arrived, I was soaking wet and the match was almost over.

sentences.text: Leo mi ha dato un asciugamano e una fetta di pizza.
sentences.meaning: Leo gave me a towel and a slice of pizza.

sentences.text: Negli ultimi minuti la Lazio ha pareggiato.
sentences.meaning: In the last few minutes Lazio equalised.

sentences.text: Alla fine ho visto solo cinque minuti di partita, e nemmeno un gol della Roma.
sentences.meaning: In the end I saw only five minutes of the match, and not even one Roma goal.

exercises.prompt: Dove voleva guardare la partita Marco?
Perché Marco è andato a piedi?
options: Perché la casa di Leo era vicina.

exercises.prompt: Che cosa è successo mentre camminava?

exercises.explain: La Lazio ha pareggiato: the match ended in a draw.

exercises.prompt: Alla fine, che cosa è piaciuto a Marco?
